en.name: Honorius I
en.summary: A pope posthumously condemned as a heretic by an ecumenical council for his ambiguous letters on the Monothelite controversy over Christ's will.
en.body: Honorius I was an energetic builder and administrator, but his lasting historical notoriety comes from his correspondence with the Patriarch of Constantinople during the Monothelite controversy, over whether Christ possessed one will or two; his letters were read as endorsing the Monothelite position. Decades after his death, the Third Council of Constantinople (680–681) formally condemned him for heresy, an unusual posthumous censure of a pope that would later be cited in debates over papal infallibility.
